entries.concept: Retro mountain soundscape with a microphone sun and boxed pop icon
entries.scene: A hand-pulled screenprinted gig poster shows one dominant central motif: a giant circular vintage microphone transformed into a striped eclipse-like sun rising from a mountain meadow. Its ring frame becomes the main halo, and inside the disc the mesh is simplified into bold horizontal bands, with black bird silhouettes cutting across it. Nestled at the base of the microphone-sun is a small open wooden box, cracked wide like a stage hatch, with a stylized adult figure unfolding from it in a fluid crouch; the figure’s face is rendered in punchy pop-art planes with dark hair, black sunglasses, and magenta lips. Orbiting this center are chunky screenprinted graphics: a deep blue biomorphic shape and a hot pink twin shape sweeping like mirrored comet shards through the sky; a continuous-line embracing couple reinterpreted as a glowing contour cut into the clouds and meadow stream; and scattered oversized keyboard-key blocks embedded like stepping stones across the foreground grid-meets-landscape plain. The whole world merges alpine valley, retro grid horizon, and poster-flat studio space into one connected environment, using thick inks, crisp knockouts, and halftone shadows so every motif reads instantly as one bold concert poster image.

entries.shootDirection: a graffiti-covered back alley, the group mid-conversation walking toward a doorway camera - candid, not posed
entries.concept: Graffiti alley doorway walk-up, tight candid group portrait
entries.scene: In a narrow graffiti-covered back alley at blue hour, the four selected artists are caught mid-conversation walking toward a metal side doorway just a few steps from the camera, framed tightly enough that every face is large, crisp, and detailed while their bodies overlap naturally in motion. On the left, the young woman in the white shirt and black tie turns slightly inward as if listening, her dark hair bouncing softly; beside her, the auburn-haired woman in sculptural glasses and a dark outfit leans forward half a step, speaking with an intent but warm expression. Slightly deeper in the frame, the dark-haired man in the black high-neck top glances sideways toward them rather than at the lens, one shoulder brushing the tagged brick wall, while on the right the masked figure with bleached hair emerges through a haze of cool doorway light, the glowing X-eyed mask adding a surreal note against otherwise real street styling. The alley is damp and softly reflective, the pastel grade muting the spray-paint reds and blues into chalky tones, with diffused dusk light from above and a faint spill from the doorway creating calm contrast instead of harsh drama; the group feels intimate, unscripted, and genuinely in the same moment rather than posed in a lineup.

entries.concept: Riverside cafe street under a striped sky of memory and reflection
entries.scene: An off-white risograph poster shows a nocturnal riverside street that turns into an open-air cafe and record-transfer workshop in one continuous setting, with a strong diagonal running from lower left to upper right. In the lower left, a simplified scooter with a cluster of round mirrors is parked at the curb, its mirrors catching tiny flat face silhouettes and its exhaust becoming grainy clouds that drift upward across the whole image. Those clouds merge into a striped evening sky made of broad horizontal bands borrowed from the warm striped portrait, overprinted so the orange and yellow become a glowing dusk behind deep blue. Along the diagonal cobblestone path, three coat-clad adult walkers move uphill past cafe windows and sparse reeds, their steps echoing the street scene while one elongated standing figure in a sweater vest leans near the edge of the pavement like a watchful passerby. At mid-right, the diner and street blend together: a counter window opens onto the cobbles, where a pompadoured tattooed man and a dark-haired woman appear as separate seated silhouettes inside, framed by condiment shapes and booth backs rather than posed portraits. Above them, pinned to a cafe awning and partly dissolving into the smoke, a doubled downward-looking curly-haired face becomes a pasted billboard image, printed as two near-identical panels. In the upper right, a large translucent production sheet hangs like a shop sign or drafting screen over the street, carrying a blue line-drawn suited figure, registration crosses, arrows, and technical boxes, as if the whole neighborhood is being mapped in real time. Reeds cut into the sky at the far edges, tying the street to the open air. Everything is reduced to bold flat shapes, halftone grain, and slight misregistration in sunflower yellow, burnt orange, and cobalt blue inks.

entries.shootDirection: the group crossing a zebra crossing toward the camera, shot square-on from across the road
entries.concept: Blue-hour city zebra crossing outside an old cinema
entries.scene: At blue hour on a broad zebra crossing outside an old cinema corner in a quiet city center, the four selected figures move toward the camera as the photographer stands square-on from the opposite curb, framed tight enough from mid-thigh up that every face stays large, crisp, and fully readable while the white stripes rush beneath them; the dark-haired man in the severe coat with fur collar leads slightly from the left with his chin turned off to one side, the young man in the red-white-blue top is half a step nearer the lens and glances back directly with one arm swinging into the foreground, the silver-haired man in the blazer walks a touch behind with his profile catching the cool ambient sky glow, and the central moustached figure in the dark suit and white tie cuts through the middle stripe line with a poised, almost theatrical stride. Storefront glass and a glowing marquee reflect soft streetlights behind them, the road still faintly damp so it picks up honest highlights, and their styling feels naturally mixed rather than coordinated: tailored dark outerwear beside sportier knitwear, all held together by the clean, true-to-life evening colour and the sense of a real caught crossing rather than a posed lineup.

entries.concept: Midnight shopwindow constellations in thawing winter
entries.creativeDirection: A layered cut-paper and screenprint collage turns urban night into a symbolic storefront diorama with hand-drawn celestial marks.
entries.scene: Street-corner viewpoint at night, looking slightly upward across a fisheye-bent shop window on a slushy winter block, with the glass acting like a stage and sky at once.

elements.element: a tiny bouquet of white daisies pinned near the top of the shop window like a fragile talisman against the night
a black-and-white dog seated on a snowbank at the curb in the foreground, beneath three bright floating emblems reimagined as window-hung signs: tiger head, bursting firecracker, and geometric star
a hand-drawn shooting star with trailing arcs scratched across the dark green-black sky reflection in the glass
a purple branching cloud of filaments and specks blooming from the left side of the storefront awning into the air like neon pollen or electrical frost
the four band members reduced to a single poster-like black-and-white silhouette grouping visible inside against an interior brick wall, appearing only once as one unified image
the overall fisheye corner-shop architecture, angled windows, receding sidewalk, and distorted urban perspective

elements.element: A single seated man in a vivid red armchair placed slightly left of center as the dominant grounded figure, with a pale plank-wall fragment and hanging hat turned into part of the stage set behind him.
A huge glowing white disc as the rear backdrop moon, with a tiny black island silhouette in the water near it and a flock of birds arcing up toward the upper right.
Two small figures standing together on a rust-colored leaf-strewn path at the edge of the jungle midground beneath heavy stormlike cloud flats.
Large foreshortened cut-paper hands reaching in from the right foreground, threaded among hanging white star ornaments.
The main environment: dense tropical foliage, river water, a white wading bird, distant elephants, and a crocodile near the front waterline.

entries.concept: Backstage shrine in a cosmic rehearsal hall
entries.creativeDirection: A handcrafted mixed-media diorama photographed like an editorial stage set, combining sculptural assemblage, paper cut graphics, and vintage portrait tableaux.
entries.scene: A wide view into a theatrical rehearsal hall transformed into a surreal shrine-like set, seen straight on at slightly elevated eye level, with a central altar-platform and layered backstage space receding behind it.

elements.element: A single soft, luminous woman in a long white vintage dress stands at the altar, lifting a small doll upward as if offering it to the room's strange machinery.
A large minimal cat face appears as a painted emblem on a hanging circular panel high in the set, watching over the scene.
The walls and platform edges are built from dense collage fragments of knobs, speakers, cables, and motion-blur photographs, creating a kinetic sound-engine environment.
A smiling silver-haired woman in a bright striped sleeveless top appears once at stage right beside a green chair and mirror, caught mid-gesture like a lively backstage host.
The impact motif becomes a torn-paper burst and dented percussion surface on the left side of the stage, suggesting explosive rhythm rather than literal violence.
Three elegantly dressed women in monochrome are restaged as a formal black-and-white portrait tableau seated around a small table in the rear left, like a framed living photograph within the set.
A spiked ritual mask forms the altar's central sculptural backdrop, looming behind the woman like a radiant sacred speaker icon.
A retro UFO with a pink tractor beam hangs above, beaming down onto a tiny astronaut figurine suspended over the altar.

entries.concept: Open-air gallery around a sunken chair
entries.creativeDirection: A tactile mixed-media diorama rendered as painted collage and weathered assemblage, balancing folk illustration with surreal photographic perspective.
entries.scene: A wide 16:9 view across a shallow circular pit in an open park clearing, seen slightly from above so the pit reads like an outdoor gallery stage sunk into the ground.

elements.element: A bold stack of overlapping blue and yellow circles becomes a vertical sculptural sign at the left edge, with black linear dividers echoed in nearby panel structures.
A back-facing visitor stands at the rim of the pit studying a row of propped display panels arranged like an impromptu exhibition.
The ground, pit walls, and display surfaces are built from distressed cream plaster textures with rust drips and embedded wire-like strands.
Five long-haired men appear only once, leaning over the circular pit from above, their hands gripping the rim to create a dramatic ring of faces against the sky.
At the bottom center of the pit sits a mustard-yellow chair on a green rug scattered with blue rectangular tiles, acting as the visual anchor.
A young woman in a knit hat stands among the trees holding a blank wooden signboard like a quiet park attendant or guide.

An ornate gold frame leans among the exhibition panels on the right, containing layered fragments of patterned costume and theatrical presence without introducing additional separate figures outside it.
A monochrome close-up portrait on one display panel shows a smiling man presenting a melting ice cream cone toward the viewer.

entries.mood: curious, handmade, slightly uncanny, sunlit yet archival

A large golden sun with a human face crowns the entire scene from above, with a few floating hearts, leaves, birds, and abstract celestial marks dispersed sparingly around it.

entries.concept: Rooftop observatory of portraits and signals
entries.creativeDirection: A hand-built mixed-media diorama photographed like a cinematic miniature, combining painted backdrops, cut-paper collage, and sculptural objects.
entries.scene: A twilight rooftop observatory garden seen from a slightly elevated frontal viewpoint, where a weathered urban roof has been transformed into a listening deck overlooking distant mountains and sky.

elements.element: A single green-cast chest-up portrait of the young man appears as the main live figure, standing among rooftop plants in a white collared shirt with a dark shoulder strap and a long narrow rod-like object angled across the foreground.
A wide illuminated rectangular sign hangs above a narrow shelf displaying three small framed male portraits as curated objects on the observatory wall.
Tinted cyan and pink photo fragments plus two black-and-white candid image scraps are reworked into pinned collage panels and translucent overlays around the wall and parapet.
A worn rooftop access door is styled like a bar entrance, with a suited man in hat at the threshold lighting a cigarette and a woman glimpsed through a small side window.
Oversized keyboard keys become stepping platforms and planters scattered across shallow reflective puddles on the roof, leading the eye toward distant alpine mountains.

Two tailored figures lounging on low black chairs occupy a secondary seating nook, accented by a translucent pink circular disc behind them, with the woman’s red shoes and the man’s bright blue suit and pink socks preserved.
A toy-like rocket with a grinning face streaks across the upper sky like a hanging mobile or animated cutout, leaving a glowing trail among starbursts.
A monumental speaker tower rises beyond the parapet as the far focal architecture, with tiny climbers, hovering helicopters, tall plants, and a red sun-disc framing the skyline.
